1   Overview

Objective: Predict DRAM wafer die failures before electrical test completion using 36 semiconductor process & test features — enabling proactive yield management at production scale (50K wafers/month).

Domain: Semiconductor Manufacturing — Memory (DRAM) Yield Engineering

Target Variable: is_fail (binary) — 0.63% positive rate (1:159 class imbalance)

Scale: 16M rows × 36 features — production-representative dataset size

Model: HybridTransformerCNN (317,633 parameters) — Transformer for tabular features + CNN for spatial wafer patterns + Fusion MLP

Infrastructure: AWS g4dn.xlarge (T4 GPU) · Apache Airflow DAGs · MLflow PostgreSQL · S3 artifacts · Docker Compose · 40-day AWS production run

This project demonstrates production-grade MLOps — not a tutorial. Real design decisions include: why bfloat16 over float16 on A100, why T4 over A100 for daily retrains, how to detect drift reliably with <10K samples, and how to build an auto-GPU selector that scales from T4 to A100 based on model complexity and data volume.

Final live AWS status (July 17, 2026): the scheduled AWS daily pipeline completed the intended 40 days, then a workflow guard bug allowed unintended Days 41-45 to run. S3 state is current_day=46, last_completed_day=45, and status=complete. The active champion remains s3://p053-mlflow-artifacts/models/day30_v2_retrained.pt. The daily cron is disabled, expensive workflow steps are guarded by should_run, EC2 and RDS are stopped, and no NAT gateways are active. Remaining billable inventory: 125 GiB gp3 EBS, 20 GiB RDS storage, 21 automated RDS snapshots, ~4.80 GB current S3 data with 387 object versions, one ECR repo, and one associated public IPv4/EIP. Retention decision: keep minimal evidence resources for now.

3   System Architecture

The system architecture shows the complete MLOps pipeline: raw DRAM process data flows through a 40-day Apache Airflow production run, triggering HybridTransformerCNN retraining on AWS g4dn.xlarge (T4 GPU) when triple drift detection (PSI + KL + KS) confirms distribution shift. MLflow tracks every experiment against the PostgreSQL RDS backend; the FastAPI inference server exposes predictions at 600 req/s throughput; Prometheus + Grafana provide real-time monitoring with a $200 CloudWatch billing alarm as the cost safety net.

The deployment stack layers the full production system: EC2 g4dn.xlarge hosts Docker Compose with Airflow (GPU scheduler), MLflow (RDS backend + S3 artifacts), FastAPI (model serving), and monitoring (Prometheus + Grafana). The GPU auto-selector dynamically routes training to T4 (our 317K model), V100, A10G, or A100 based on model parameter count and data volume — a design that scales without manual intervention.

4   Results
Champion Model: HybridTransformerCNN (317,633 params) · AUC-ROC: 0.816 · AUC-PR: 0.054 (vs 0.006 random baseline) · F1: 0.127 · Training: 50 epochs on A100 in 201.7 min (Colab Pro, Day 1)
4.1   Exploratory Data Analysis

Class distribution across train/val/test/unseen splits, confirming consistent 0.63% positive rate (1:159 imbalance). The stratified sampling ensures no data leakage while maintaining realistic fail ratios in every partition — critical for fair evaluation at production imbalance.

Spatial wafer heatmap showing die failure rates across X/Y positions. Edge dice exhibit 3.2× higher failure probability due to lithography edge effects and CMP gradient variations — a physically motivated spatial signal that the CNN branches of HybridTransformerCNN are designed to capture.

Feature correlation heatmap across all 36 features, revealing which electrical test parameters carry the strongest linear signal. Retention-temperature interaction and leakage-retention ratio show the highest correlation with is_fail, validating the domain-engineered feature choices.

PCA projection of 16M samples shows partial class separability in the first two principal components. The overlap confirms that linear decision boundaries are insufficient — motivating the nonlinear HybridTransformerCNN architecture over simpler logistic regression approaches.

Feature distribution comparison between pass and fail dice for key electrical test parameters. Several features show bimodal distributions with clear separation between pass and fail populations — particularly cell_leakage_fa and retention_time_ms — confirming that the model has learnable signal across multiple feature dimensions simultaneously.

4.2   Baseline Models

Precision-Recall curves for all baseline models on the validation set. AUC-PR is the primary metric for this imbalanced problem (1:159). XGBoost achieves AUC-PR=0.031, substantially above the random baseline of 0.006, establishing the bar that HybridTransformerCNN must exceed.

XGBoost feature importance (gain) ranking the top predictors. cell_leakage_fa and retention_time_ms top the list, consistent with domain knowledge that charge leakage and retention are the primary failure mechanisms in DRAM. The engineered features (leakage_retention_ratio, edge_risk) rank significantly higher than raw electrical test values, validating the domain feature engineering.

4.3   HybridTransformerCNN — A100 Day 1 Training
bfloat16 Critical Fix: float16 + GradScaler caused a gradient death spiral on A100 — GradScaler scale → 0, all gradients became zero, loss collapsed to constant. Root cause: FocalLoss at 1:159 imbalance produces gradient magnitudes that overflow float16's 5-bit exponent. Fix: switched to bfloat16 (8-bit exponent) WITHOUT GradScaler. Fixed in 11 locations across 7 files. This is a known A100/CUDA 12.1 behavior documented in PyTorch issue #84730.

Training and validation curves over 50 epochs on NVIDIA A100 (40GB). Loss decreases steadily without the GradScaler collapse seen in earlier float16 runs. AUC-ROC improves from 0.5 (random) at epoch 1 to 0.816 at epoch 50, with AUC-PR showing the characteristic slow improvement expected with severe class imbalance — FocalLoss focusing on the 0.63% minority samples drives meaningful gradient signal despite sparsity.

Day 1 A100 training summary — 50 epochs, 201.7 minutes (NB03 Production Notebook). Final metrics: Val AUC-ROC=0.816, AUC-PR=0.054, F1=0.127. Model saved as day1_champion.pt and uploaded to S3 (s3://p053-mlflow-artifacts/models/day1_champion.pt) for retrieval by production Airflow DAGs.

Precision-Recall curve for HybridTransformerCNN showing AUC-PR=0.054 — a 9× improvement over the random baseline (0.006). In a fab environment, the operating point is tuned by the yield engineer: high-precision threshold minimizes false alarms (expensive rework), high-recall threshold maximizes wafer capture (revenue protection). The AUC-PR allows selection of any operating point on this curve.

4.4   Hardware Benchmarks

Hardware benchmark comparing throughput (samples/sec) and epoch time across Apple MPS (M1), NVIDIA T4 (g4dn.xlarge), and NVIDIA A100. The A100 delivers ~80,000–120,000 samples/sec vs T4's ~19,000 vs MPS's ~1,800. For daily production retraining on 5M rows, T4 trains 1 epoch in ~4.4 minutes — meeting the 24-hour SLA easily. The A100 was used only for the initial 50-epoch Day 1 champion model; all subsequent retrains run on T4 at $0.53/hr vs $4.10/hr for A100.

4.5   Model Comparison

AUC-PR comparison across all model families: Logistic Regression (0.009), Random Forest (0.022), XGBoost (0.031), and HybridTransformerCNN (0.054). The hybrid model's 9× improvement over the random baseline (0.006) is significant but the absolute value reflects the genuine difficulty of a 1:159 imbalanced problem — a realistic outcome, not an inflated number. SHAP analysis confirms the model captures non-linear interactions between spatial position, temperature, and leakage that tree models cannot.

Confusion matrices at optimal threshold for XGBoost vs HybridTransformerCNN on the test set. HybridTransformerCNN achieves better recall (fewer missed failures) at comparable False Positive Rate — critical in semiconductor manufacturing where a missed failure costs $5K+ in downstream processing of bad wafers.

Generalization analysis comparing train, validation, test, and unseen split performance. The small gap between train/val/test and unseen metrics confirms the model is not overfitting — the 10M training samples provide sufficient regularization. Production generalization is expected to hold within ±3% AUC-ROC for data from the same process node.

4.6   Unseen Data Performance
Generalization Test: 2M completely held-out samples (different random seed, never seen during training or validation). AUC-ROC degradation <2% from test set — confirms production readiness.
4.7   MLOps Pipeline & Drift Monitoring

40-day drift monitoring timeline showing PSI (Population Stability Index) values across all major feature groups. Stable period (Days 1–19), moderate drift onset (Day 20, PSI=0.12), severe drift (Day 31, PSI=0.28 — exceeding the 0.25 retrain threshold), and recovery (Day 39). The triple detection system (PSI + KL divergence + KS test) prevents false positive retrain triggers from single-metric noise.

Retrain gate decision logic: three independent drift signals must ALL exceed thresholds before triggering retraining. Days with <10K samples are automatically tagged as drift_reliable=false and suppressed from retrain decisions — preventing the system from acting on statistically unreliable PSI estimates during data ramp-up periods.

PSI waterfall chart breaking down drift contribution by feature group across the 40-day timeline. Electrical test features (cell_leakage_fa, retention_time_ms) show the earliest and largest drift signals, consistent with process recipe changes at Day 20. Spatial features remain stable throughout, confirming the drift is process-origin, not equipment or data acquisition.

40-day production run summary showing daily data volume growth (5M rows/day at full scale), the Day 30 retrain/promotion event, the Day 39 canary failure and rollback path, model version progression, and champion versus challenger decisions. The intended live AWS daily pipeline completed through Day 40; a later schedule guard bug produced extra Days 41-45 and was fixed by disabling cron plus guarding expensive workflow steps.

Grafana monitoring dashboard showing real-time model performance metrics: prediction latency (p50/p95/p99), inference throughput (req/s), drift PSI trend, and model version indicator. The 600 req/s peak throughput at p99 latency <12ms meets the fab's real-time tester integration SLA.

Retrain event story: champion model AUC-PR before and after the adaptive retrain path. The Day 30 v2 retrain recovers degraded drift performance and becomes champion after canary evaluation. Day 39 exercises the bad-model/canary failure path, and the system keeps or rolls back to the v2 champion instead of promoting a worse model.

4.8   Deployment & Cost Analysis

Total cost breakdown for the complete 40-day production run on AWS: EC2 g4dn.xlarge is billed only while running, RDS db.t3.micro should be stopped when idle, S3 bills by retained GB-month, and public IPv4/EIP, snapshots, EBS/RDS storage, or CloudWatch logs can continue small residual charges. The July 17 audit verified EC2 stopped, RDS stopped, no active NAT gateways, and the daily workflow schedule disabled, with these retained resources still present: 125 GiB gp3 EBS, 20 GiB RDS storage, 21 automated RDS snapshots, ~4.80 GB current S3 data with 387 object versions, one ECR repo, and one associated public IPv4/EIP. They are intentionally kept as minimal evidence for now.

Load test results for the FastAPI inference server running on g4dn.xlarge: 600 req/s sustained throughput, p50 latency 3ms, p95 latency 8ms, p99 latency 12ms. The PyTorch model runs in bfloat16 inference mode, reducing VRAM usage 2× vs float32. Horizontal scaling to 8 pods (HPA configuration) would handle 4,800 req/s — sufficient for a 200K wafer/day fab running parallel testers.

5   AWS Production Infrastructure
Principle: EVERYTHING on AWS. Zero MacBook. Zero Colab for retrains. All data on S3. All experiments tracked in MLflow PostgreSQL RDS. Auto-stop EC2 + RDS + NAT Gateway after the production run completes. CloudWatch billing alarm at $200 USD.

7   Key Learnings & Interview Stories
  • bfloat16 is not optional on A100 with FocalLoss: float16 + GradScaler causes a gradient death spiral at 1:159 imbalance. The 8-bit exponent of bfloat16 (vs 5-bit float16) handles the large gradient dynamic range. Fixed in 11 locations across 7 files — a production debugging experience interviewers at NVIDIA will recognize immediately.
  • Auto-GPU selector scales the system: Our 317K model always runs on T4 ($0.53/hr). But the selector auto-detects when model complexity (>1.2B params) or data volume (>1B rows) requires A100 ($32.77/hr). Data volume matters because T4's 320 GB/s HBM bandwidth can't feed the DataLoader at 1B+ rows — a hardware bottleneck most tutorials never mention.
  • Drift detection with <10K samples is unreliable: PSI at <10K has high variance — a 0.25 PSI might be noise. Solution: compute drift for all days (full observability), but tag low-data days as drift_reliable=false and suppress retrain. Auditors see everything; the system stays honest.
  • AWS GPU quota defaults to zero: New accounts cannot launch G-family instances until a Service Quotas increase is approved. In enterprise, these are pre-negotiated with AWS account teams during the annual commit. Lesson: always request quota increases before project kick-off, not during deployment.
  • Two Docker Compose files is the right pattern: Development uses LocalStack + local PostgreSQL + no GPU. Production uses real S3 + RDS + NVIDIA runtime. Maintaining both eliminates the "works on my machine" problem without exposing production credentials during development.
  • Auto-stop infrastructure is not an afterthought: ec2_auto_stop.py stops EC2 + RDS + NAT gateway and sends a CloudWatch alarm when the 40-day production run finishes. Without this, a $0.53/hr instance running for a month costs about $380. With it, compute charges stop after the run; the remaining closeout task is deleting or lifecycle-expiring retained S3, EBS/RDS, log, snapshot, and public IPv4 resources if the goal is near-zero ongoing AWS cost.
